chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from some of our companions, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), who said:
When the wife who has not been entered into (consummated) is divorced, she becomes free from the marriage bond by a single pronouncement.
ai.seo_question: How many divorce pronouncements are required to divorce a wife before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar, this hadith clarifies that for a wife not yet consummated with, a single pronouncement of talaq is sufficient to effect separation, a ruling derived from the absence of the waiting period (iddah) complexities found in post-consummation cases. This aligns with the Shia juristic view that the 'one divorce' rule applies here, distinguishing it from the three-divorce structure mandated after consummation. The narration underscores the simplicity of the legal process when the marital bond has not been fully actualized through physical intimacy.
